title: Samsung's Six Affiliates to Invest $1B in KKR's Helix AI Infrastructure Platform
content:
Korea Supply Chain Brief · September 29, 2026

Six Samsung Group affiliates — Samsung Electronics, Samsung C&T, Samsung SDS, Samsung SDI, Samsung Life Insurance and Samsung Fire & Marine Insurance — will jointly invest US$1 billion (about KRW 1.36 trillion) in Helix Digital Infrastructure, a U.S. company founded by global investment firm KKR to build the physical backbone of the AI industry. Here is what was announced and what Helix actually builds.

Samsung Electronics

What was announced

  • Total investment: US$1 billion, about KRW 1.36 trillion.
  • Split: Samsung Electronics alone puts in $500 million; the other five affiliates — Samsung C&T, Samsung SDS, Samsung SDI, Samsung Life Insurance and Samsung Fire & Marine Insurance — contribute a combined $500 million.
  • Target: Helix Digital Infrastructure, launched in June this year by KKR, a major U.S. global investment firm.

What Helix actually builds

Helix is not a data center operator alone. According to the announcement, it provides an integrated set of physical infrastructure the AI industry needs: developing and operating hyperscale data centers, plus the power generation, transmission and distribution, and fiber-optic network buildout that feed them. That combination — compute, power and connectivity bundled into one platform — is the specific thing Samsung's six affiliates are buying into, rather than a single data center project.

Why this cuts across six different Samsung businesses

The investor list spans electronics, construction/trading (Samsung C&T), IT services (Samsung SDS), batteries (Samsung SDI) and two insurers (Samsung Life, Samsung Fire & Marine). A financial stake in AI infrastructure is a different kind of exposure for each: for Samsung Electronics it sits alongside its chip and server hardware business, while for the two insurers it reads as a portfolio investment seeking stable, infrastructure-like returns rather than an operational move.

What is not disclosed

  • Samsung's ownership stake or board rights in Helix, if any.
  • Which specific data center or power projects the capital will fund first.
  • Whether any Samsung affiliate will also supply equipment or services to Helix's buildout.

Quick FAQ

How much is Samsung investing and in what?
US$1 billion (about KRW 1.36 trillion) across six Samsung affiliates, into Helix Digital Infrastructure, a KKR-founded company building AI data centers and the power/network infrastructure around them.

Which Samsung company is putting in the most?
Samsung Electronics, at $500 million — half of the total.

Is this the same as Samsung supplying chips or servers to a customer?
No. This is a financial investment in an infrastructure company, not a disclosed supply agreement.
